This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $f(k)$ be the minimal $N$ such that if $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is $k$-coloured then there is a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$. Estimate $f(k)$. In particular, is it true that $f(k) < c^k$ for some constant $c>0$?
#483: [Er61,p.233][Er65,p.188]
number theory | 
additive combinatorics | 
ramsey theory
The values of $f(k)$ are known as Schur numbers. The best-known bounds for large $k$ are\[(380)^{k/5}-O(1)\leq f(k) \leq (e-\tfrac{1}{6}) k!.\]Note that $380^{1/5}\approx 3.2806$. The lower bound is due to Ageron, Casteras, Pellerin, Portella, Rimmel, and Tomasik [ACPPRT21] (improving previous bounds of Exoo [Ex94] and Fredricksen and Sweet [FrSw00]). The upper bound is due to Xu, Xie, and Chen [XXC02] (improving previous bounds of Wan [Wa97] and Whitehead [Wh73]). See Eliahou [El20] for more on the upper bound.
The known values of $f$ are $f(1)=2$, $f(2)=5$, $f(3)=14$, $f(4)=45$, and $f(5)=161$ (see A030126). (The equality $f(5)=161$ was established by Heule [He17]).
See also [183] (in particular a folklore observation gives $f(k)\leq R(3;k)-1$).
Additional thanks to: Desmond Weisenberg and Wouter Cames van Batenburg

 The constant in the upper bound has also been improved slightly via R(3;k). Wan (1997) proved $R(3;k)\leq \tfrac{e−e^{-1}+3}{2}\cdot k!+1$, and Xu Xiaodong, Xie Zheng and Chen Zhi (2002) improved this to $R(3;k) \leq (e−\tfrac{1}{6})\cdot k!+1$. The latter paper is in Chinese and I haven't been able to open the file, but Eliahou (2019) contains a write-up in English, along with some bounds conditional on improvements for small k.

 Same comment as for problem 183:
The mentioned base of the lower bound $(321)^{1/5}\approx 3.1717$ of Exoo (1994) was improved to $(1073)^{1/6} \approx3.1996$ by Fredericksen and Sweet (2000) doi:10.37236/1510 via $f(6)\geq 536$. 
Both papers used that $\lim_{k \rightarrow \infty}f(k)^{1/k} \geq (2 f(m)+1)^{1/m}$ for every positive integer $m$; see e.g. Corollary 2.1 in Abbott and Hanson (1972).
The current best lower bound is in a preprint of Ageron, Casteras, Pellerin, Portella, Rimmel and Tomasik (2021) doi:10.48550/arXiv.2112.03175, where they find $\lim_{k \rightarrow \infty} f(k)^{1/k} \geq (380)^{1/5} \approx
 3.2806\ldots$
